objective: Qualify capacity ceiling changes, maintenance and turnover as non-evicting aggregate state transitions, and preserve the distinction between unknown/unavailable capacity and zero demand.
steps: Add focused cases for closure with active reservations/occupancy, maintenance marking/restoration, work-to-cleaning-to-free turnover, and zero demand versus known-zero/unknown capacity.
Run the focused capacity contract to observe the expected missing-method failure before implementation.
Implement checked aggregate disposition transitions and ceiling updates that preserve active counts; do not add scheduling, identity, or grant arbitration.
Run focused capacity tests, core clippy and formatting checks.

verification.oracle: Capacity and lifecycle contract tests pass, including non-eviction and transition conservation.
All careops-core targets pass clippy with warnings denied.

acceptance: Closure or staffing ceiling changes preserve reserved, occupied and cleaning counts even when no new capacity remains.
Maintenance and turnover transitions conserve equipped units, reject underflow/overflow, and leave state unchanged on rejected transitions.
Known-zero capacity with positive demand is distinct from zero demand and from unknown capacity.
No allocation arbitration, ED schema/default change, Kairos edit, dependency or lockfile change.
stop_conditions: Transition requires resource identity or grant arbitration
